photos.c: Wearing the English Rose, M40 Jim Estall (220) grafts away at the head of the Home Countries International Veterans' Cross Country Champs. at Ballymena on November 8th.  It's the fourth of  five laps and still no-one has been able to dominate the field.  However, the tattooed Rob Wise, close up behind Jim at this point, was soon to make a decisive move.  Gerry Brady (211) of Ireland was unable to respond while Mike Hagar and Jim gave chase.  On the final lap the Belgravian overtook Hagar to gain a clear 2nd in 31:55 but Wise at 31:37 was out of reach.

photos.c:
Left Derrick Williams - our talented all rounder here seen in the 100 x 1 mile relay.
Right Stuart Paton who tops this year's 1500m Club Rankings.

TEAM SPIRIT

Tremendous team spirit has been a key feature off all the British League fixtures this year. When Pat Lyttle put in his best performance to date in winning the 'B' string 100m and 200m at the Warley meeting the first to congratulate him was jumps Captain Derrick Williams. This picture records Derricks only moment of inactivity as he amassed 30 points from; High Jump, Long Jump, Triple Jump, 100m and 400m Relay Squads.

Our victorious team after their outstanding win in the Wellington Relays held on the race course at Ostend.
Back row left to right; Mike Alleyne, Derrick Williams, Guy Sagar, Pat Lyttle, Dave Mote, Gary Staines, John Gladwin, Kevin Sturman, Richard Addison, and Mark Sinclair.
Front row left to right; Paul Richley, Stuart Paton, Oliver Foote, and Team Manager - Leo Coy.

One of the highlights of this years British League was the close dual between our triple jump specialists Dr,Aham Amadi(left) and Mr. Derrick Williams, which Aham won 3-1. Aham and Derrick won between them every A&B Triple Jump at all four British League matches.

Derrick Williams all-round talents have never been in doubt. Over the years he has been our 'A' string in the 100m, 200m, LJ, HJ, TJ and part of the 4 x 100 and 4 x 400 squads. He has even won the Surrey Decathlon Championship. In our last BAL Div.2 Match at Battersea he ran his first 400m Hurdles more of a series of hops if this photo is to be believed - and recorded a quite remarkable 55sec. in his debut. What if he took it seriously and cleared the hurdle and not the railings.
Jumping With style! Derrick Williams immaculate technique has now been captured in a series of coaching videos made for the I.F.A. which is to be distributed to over 140 Countries.

It would be hard to find a first team man with greater enthusiasm for Belgrave and a feature of the season has been the support of our British League efforts by Terry and his family. Terry has helped the field men to hold their own in terms of points gained and he and Bill Treharne have together added respectability to the hammer. Sadly Terry is to join his Battalion early in 1984 and it looks as though we will be losing his services next season. Thanks for your support Terry. We look forward to your return to our ranks.

BELGRAVE CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS 1987.
Frank Ward(8) Winner of 10 Miles Senior, Martin Lake Runner Up in both 7½ and 10 Miles Senior races and Richard Blick (2) Winner of Youths race and Matthew Egerickx(7) Winner of the Boys Championship.

Left: Paul Evans (1) drifts to the front of the pack before turning up the heat. He took the A race comfortably in the first two BAL 5000m races, backed up well by Frank Ward (2), also shown left, in match 1 and Ollie Foote in match 2.

Above: Top left to right - Ollie Foote, second Belgravian home at Coulsdon, a hirsute Frank Ward (we hear he has taken it off for his wedding) and Marco Mazzotta., who has steadily improved since last Autumn. Bottom - Jon Hobbs, Andy Paton and Don Anderson, the man who runs the Club '10' and then goes round again to collect the flags (and probably went round before to set them up!

Opposite page: The "last" Belgrave-Southern Relay.
Top. High noon and the starter sends 61 runners off on the first leg. Jon Hobbs completes his lap of the "top" and nears the crowd at the Hand in Hand.
Centre. Ollie Foote sends Marcello Bizio away on the last stage. Jim Estall loosens up for the London Marathon with a 25:53 long leg. Second fastest long stage of the day and another mark in the all-time top 20 - Paul Evans has an easy run!
Bottom. Jim Estall launches Marco Mazzotta. Frank Ward reaches the summit of Wool Road. Putting on a good show for visiting relations, "Aussie" Brandon Reid streaks off the Common for a nippy second leg.
Above: Frank Ward has spent the winter gradually regaining fitness and will be wanting to get well under 15 minutes again for 5,000m this summer.

photos.c: Belgrave's Winning AAA 12-Stage Team at Sutton Park. Back row: Andy Graffin, Spencer Barden, Paul Freary, Stephen Sharp, Alaster Stewart, David Anderson, Allen Graffin, Paul Evans. Front row: Lee Hurst, Mark Miles, Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward, Charles Herrington.

Above (1): Belgrave's men retained the AAA 6-Stage Road Relay Championship at Sutton Park in October 2002. Mark Miles, Richard Ward, Spencer Barden, Stephen Sharp, Allen Graffin and David Anderson celebrate keeping hold of the trophy for another year. This is the hardest team title to win - can they make it three in a row in October 2003?
Top right: Richard Ward came into the team as reserve on the Friday and proceeded to demonstrate that he should have been in the dozen in the first place!

Bottom right: The victorious Belgrave crew can't stop smiling after retaining their title. Standing: Jonathan Blackledge (stage 6), Al Stewart (11), Kevin Nash (3), Adam Zawadski (12), Martin Dent (7), Paul Freary (1), Paul Evans (9 - and what proved to be his last team run for Belgrave), David Anderson (4). Kneeling: Allen Graffin (5), Will Cockerell (10), Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward (8), Stephen Sharp (2).

Above: The start of the Eastleigh 10k on March 19th.  The race included the CAU Inter-Counties Championship and Belgravians were racing in some unfamiliar vests.  In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind  these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).  To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent).  Maclean's winning time was 29:47, Mays was second in 30:00 and Phil Wicks 3rd in 30:02.  Belgrave won the team race and Surrey the Inter-County Championship. Full result and report in the previous issue.  Photo by Steve Wicks.
Above:  Richard Ward – “on cruise control” to bring us home to our fifth consecutive SEAA 12-Stage win.  Photo by Steve Wicks.

Above: The AAA 5k Road Race was again held in Horwich. It was only the second time the Championship has been held and the Bels have medalled on each occasion – silver in 2005 and now gold in 2006. Individual AAA Champion was Chris Davies of Telford (in the red and yellow), second was Peter Riley of Leigh (white vest with green diagonal) and third was our own Mark Miles (177). Simon Jones (not pictured) and Richard Ward (181) made up the Belgrave team. The Open race was won by Birchfield, running three Africans, but they were not eligible for the AAA race.

Happy with a seventh successive year in the medals at the National Road Relay. Standing (left to right) Gerry North, Gordon Biscoe, Bill Laws, Brian Pritchard, Tom Osment, Maureen Pritchard, Zara Chidoub, Mark Pollard, Jonathan Blackledge, Janet Blackledge, Mike Blackledge, Neil Speaight, Alan Mead, Padraic Buckley, Paul Freary, Eric Hall, Pete Willis, Hazel Mead. Front row. Mavis Hall, Charles Jones, Richard Ward, Simon Jones, Malachi Byansi, Will Cockerell, Pat Mead, Phil Wicks.

photos.c: Above: Stephen Sharp (stage 6), Phil Wicks (2), Jonathan Blackledge (5), Spencer Barden (4), Alaster Stewart (1) and Tim Watson (3) receive the Ian Logan Trophy – Belgrave’s fourth year of being top of the pile at Rushmoor Arena.  Only Stephen and Jonathan remained in the squad from 2004’s winning line-up.
“Sweatshop” Surrey CC League Race 1 at Brockwell Park, and Phil Wicks (9) and Stephen Sharp (1) slug it out at the front of the field.
With “Sweatshop” Surrey Cross Country League race less than one minute old, Phil Wicks has made clear his intentions.  He went on to claim his first league win.  Photo by Steve Wicks.
Phil Wicks laid his cards on the table at Lloyd Park, pushing on hard from the start, but it was Thames Hare & Hounds’ John McFarlane (263) who held all the aces.

Above: The start of the Eastleigh 10k on March 19th.  The race included the CAU Inter-Counties Championship and Belgravians were racing in some unfamiliar vests.  In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind  these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).  To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent).  Maclean's winning time was 29:47, Mays was second in 30:00 and Phil Wicks 3rd in 30:02.  Belgrave won the team race and Surrey the Inter-County Championship. Full result and report in the previous issue.  Photo by Steve Wicks.

Above: Start of the South of Thames Championship in Brockwell Park: Dave Anderson, Pete Willis (20), Mike Trees (18), James McMullen (Epsom Oddballs 142), Will Clark (Epsom & Ewell 137), Alan Barnes (Herne Hill 175), James Connor (Kent AC), Phil Wicks (19), Dean Lacy (Cambridge H 51), Alex Bodin.

Above: A mile gone in the men’s race and Barry Royden (847 Medway & Maidstone) holds a narrow lead with Matt Ashton (3 Aldershot F&D), Darren Deed (61 Bedford &C) and Phil Wicks (100 Belgrave) in echelon. Just behind Royden is Huw Lobb (Bedford), Dominic Bannister (Shaftesbury) and Andy Robinson (Newham & Essex Beagles).

Happy with a seventh successive year in the medals at the National Road Relay. Standing (left to right) Gerry North, Gordon Biscoe, Bill Laws, Brian Pritchard, Tom Osment, Maureen Pritchard, Zara Chidoub, Mark Pollard, Jonathan Blackledge, Janet Blackledge, Mike Blackledge, Neil Speaight, Alan Mead, Padraic Buckley, Paul Freary, Eric Hall, Pete Willis, Hazel Mead. Front row. Mavis Hall, Charles Jones, Richard Ward, Simon Jones, Malachi Byansi, Will Cockerell, Pat Mead, Phil Wicks.
Gold medals came wholesale for Phil Wicks – First in the ERRA & UKA individual championships and a member of the winning team in both championships as well.

NATIONAL 6-STAGE ROAD RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
Yes, we’ve brought you pictures like this before – but while our lads are able to notch up such great victories, we’ll have no hesitation in bringing you further such images. Left to right: James Kelly (stage 2), Phil Wicks (6), Stephen Sharp (1), Mark Miles (5), Jonathan Blackledge (3) and Simon Jones (4)

NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
A third National title of the Autumn season came Belgrave’s way at the end of a riveting race at Berry Hill Park, Mansfield. It was only the second time in our history that we’ve managed to pull this one off. Left to right: Mark Pollard (stage 2), Stephen Sharp (1), Phil Wicks (4), Mark Miles (3).
Above: Phil Wicks’ 14:46 on the final leg was on a par with Gary Staines run in 1996 and the efforts by Dave Anderson and Spencer Barden in our record breaking run of 2003.

Phil Wicks makes a fast start in the 2008 English National Cross Country Championship at Alton Towers. He placed second, only the third Belgravian in our history to do so (the others being Vic Blowfield in 1948 and Allen Graffin in 2002. Birhan Dagne has won the women’s race and Kassa Tadesse the junior men’s race – but we patiently wait for a senior men’s winner! Photo by Alan Mead.
They’ve done it again! National 6-Stage Road Relay Champions for a seventh time. Left to right above: Stephen Sharp (Captain), Nick Goolab, Steve Davies, Simon Jones, Phil Wicks, Neil Speaight.

Right: A set of medals was a possibility for the seniors but things didn’t go our way and only Phil Wicks (6197) ran up to expectations. Others pictured left to right are Mal Byansi, Russell Dessaix-Chin, Knut Hegvold, and to the right of and behind Phil – Pete Willis, Will Cockerell, James Kelly and Lander Eguia. Photos by Alan Mead.
